title: QBR / Health Check - Seacliff Retail
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage growth, rising token costs, a couple of recent latency blips during peak traffic, and next steps around benchmarking dedicated capacity and sharing security artifacts.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send detailed QBR deck and month-to-date usage/cost breakdown by 2026-05-22

Maya Rodriguez: Share 30-day token usage export and sample peak traffic windows by 2026-05-21
Samir Patel: Set up weekly check-in cadence starting 2026-05-26 and invite engineering stakeholders

Share SOC 2 report and SSO / SAML integration guide

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-19
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Maya Rodriguez (Seacliff Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Seacliff Infra Lead), Noah Bennett (Seacliff PM)

Summary (auto): quick QBR to review usage/cost trends, recent reliability blips, and next steps for pilot/dedicated sizing and security docs.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. do we have everyone on the line?
[00:05] Maya Rodriguez: yep here, thanks jordan.
[00:07] Samir Patel: hi all, samir here from cs. agenda for today: quick usage review, cost drivers, any incidents, then roadmap and security follow ups.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: perfect. priya will run through the performance and sizing notes, i'll cover commercial and usage trends.
[00:28] Priya Nair: hi team. starting with latency and error trends — overall p50 is stable at ~120ms for the hosted API, p95 spikes to 820ms during last week's 10:30am PST traffic surge. there were two short timeouts reported, both tied to burst traffic that hit our shared pool limits.
[00:48] Ethan Cole: yeah we saw that on our side, friday around 10:28 we had a couple of user flows time out which caused a retry cascade. it cost us some conversions.
[01:00] Maya Rodriguez: curious — were those retries from our side or did the client library do automatic retries?
[01:05] Samir Patel: looks like some retries from your frontend, and a couple of automatic retries when the server returned 504s.
[01:10] Jordan Lee: on the usage front, month-over-month token volume is up ~42% driven by a new product feature you shipped in early april. cost per token spiked a bit due to increased p95 length and more completions per user.
[01:25] Noah Bennett: that aligns — our new "smart search" path issues 20-30% more tokens per query. we're trying to tune prompts but also considering if we should offload some workloads to embeddings + rerank.
[01:38] Priya Nair: embeddings + rerank can reduce cost if you can trade a little latency for offline compute. we can help design a hybrid flow. also caching prefix tokens for common queries would cut repeated context.
[01:50] Maya Rodriguez: on caching — we tried the SDK cache at the app layer but it's brittle with personalization. what does redwood offer for prefix/KV caching?
[01:58] Priya Nair: we have automatic prefix caching in the runtime that stores KV caches for hot prefixes; for personalized content you can configure cache keys by session or user, and control TTLs. that has cut costs 15-30% for similar customers.
[02:12] Ethan Cole: security check — we need to confirm data residency and KMS usage for logs and any cached data. last quarter we were asked by compliance to verify that no customer PII is persisted outside our control.
[02:23] Samir Patel: we can share the KMS integration guide; for private deployments we support customer-managed keys and optional on-prem cache. for hosted env our logs are encrypted at rest and you can opt into short retention.
[02:35] Jordan Lee: i'll add that to the follow ups.
[02:40] Priya Nair: jumping back to the incident — the root cause was an under-provisioned shared pool during a region-wide burst; the runtime did fall back to a slower variant for some requests which increased latency. we recommended either increasing reserved capacity or enabling burst capacity.
[02:55] Maya Rodriguez: can you quantify cost for reserved vs burst? we don't want to overcommit monthly.
[03:00] Jordan Lee: sure — rough numbers: a small dedicated pool that covers your baseline would be about 35% higher monthly than current hosted spend but gives predictable p95 and no cross-tenant noisy neighbor issues. burst pricing is pay-as-you-go for extra capacity and can be capped. i'll send a spreadsheet with scenarios.
[03:18] Noah Bennett: ok would love the spreadsheet. also curious about the SLA changes with dedicated.
[03:23] Samir Patel: dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and lower latency targets; we'll include exact terms in the dedicated offering doc.
[03:30] Priya Nair: one more note on model selection — you mentioned in the intake that you've been using the medium-latency variant for chat. there's a lower-cost quantized variant that could be smaller token-cost per inference but slightly higher p50. could be a fit for background inference.
[03:46] Maya Rodriguez: would that affect output quality for our search completions? we have tight tolerances.
[03:50] Priya Nair: depends on prompts. we can run side-by-side evals with your real prompt set and measure delta in ROUGE/accuracy and subjective quality. we usually do a blind eval with product.
[04:02] Jordan Lee: on billing — last invoice showed a one-off network egress charge that wasn't expected. has finance reconciled that?
[04:08] Ethan Cole: yeah that was flagged, our billing team saw a line item for cross-region egress. we need a detailed invoice breakout.
[04:15] Jordan Lee: i'll get the detailed invoice export to you, samir will follow up with finance.
[04:19] Samir Patel: noted.
[04:22] [05:00] Jordan Lee: let's open the roadmap piece — next quarter we're releasing improved prefix caching controls, better KV cache observability, and a new cheaper quantized runtime option.
[05:12] Maya Rodriguez: the observability for KV cache is important, we need to audit what keys are being stored for compliance. will those logs be accessible in the console or via API?
[05:20] Priya Nair: both — console will show cache hit/miss rates per route and a table of keys hashed (not raw PII), and APIs for metrics export. for audit we can provide a hashed key map and retention controls.
[05:33] Ethan Cole: we also have a question about SSO and RBAC — we plan to use Okta, want to provision roles for dev vs prod. what's the recommended approach?
[05:40] Samir Patel: we support SAML/Okta; you can map groups to role templates. we'll send the SSO mapping guide. for dedicated and private, you get finer RBAC with org-level roles.
[05:50] Noah Bennett: any timeline on SOC2 renewal? our security team will want to see the current report.
[05:55] Jordan Lee: our SOC 2 Type II was completed in Q1 2026, i'll attach the report and summary.
[06:00] Maya Rodriguez: perfect.
[06:03] [10:00] Priya Nair: quick deep dive — if you want to pilot dedicated capacity for peak hours only, we can set up a small reserved pool with autoscale and a burst cap. test plan: 1) mirror traffic for 48 hours, 2) measure p95 and cost delta, 3) evaluate fallbacks. would need infra access to run the benchmark.
[06:25] Ethan Cole: our infra team can set up a mirror and we can provide a short-term token for the benchmark. what's the expected duration for the benchmarking?
[06:30] Priya Nair: typically 24-48 hours gives a representative window; if you have daily periodic spikes we prefer 48 hours.
[06:36] Noah Bennett: are there any special hooks we need to set up for tracing? we use datadog.
[06:40] Priya Nair: we have tracing headers and an open telemetry exporter; we'll walk you through the tracing hooks and provide a sample dashboard for datadog.
[06:48] Jordan Lee: quick question from finance — if we move to dedicated, can we do a quarterly commit instead of annual?
[06:53] Samir Patel: yes, we have quarterly reserved plans for smaller partners; discounts scale with commitment length. we'll include both in the pricing pack.
[07:00] [15:00] Maya Rodriguez: switching gears — on cost optimization, any quick wins we can implement in the next two weeks without infra work?
[07:07] Priya Nair: yes: 1) tune prompts to reduce unnecessary tokens, 2) enable route-level caching for common strings, 3) convert some workloads to embeddings + rerank, 4) evaluate quantized variant for background jobs. we can provide a prioritized list.
[07:20] Jordan Lee: we'll send a prioritized playbook with expected savings per item.
[07:25] Maya Rodriguez: great. also one operational ask — our security team wants the audit log retention extended for 13 months for compliance; what's possible?
[07:33] Samir Patel: hosted default is 90 days but we offer extended retention as an add-on; for enterprise dedicated/private we can do 13 months. i'll surface pricing.
[07:40] Ethan Cole: for the benchmark, will we need to spin up test keys or can we use a staging integration?
[07:44] Priya Nair: staging integration is fine; test keys with limited scopes are recommended. we'll provide the exact permissions needed.
[07:50] [20:00] Noah Bennett: are we tracking any regressions in generation quality after model updates? we had a small regression in january that affected our FAQ responses.
[07:58] Priya Nair: we run quality monitoring tied to prompt sets; when model upgrades happen we run canary prompts and auto-alerts for metric drift. we can ingest your prompt suite and set thresholds.
[08:08] Maya Rodriguez: we'd like to get those alerts routed to slack and to a jira queue.
[08:12] Samir Patel: supported — we'll set up integrations.
[08:15] Jordan Lee: circling back to next steps — i'll compile the QBR deck, cost scenarios, and SOC2 doc. priya will own the benchmark and run the dedicated test. samir will coordinate check-ins and billing.
[08:30] Maya Rodriguez: timeline ok — would prefer results before the end of the month if possible.
[08:35] Priya Nair: we'll do our best to get preliminary results by 2026-05-26.
[08:40] Jordan Lee: any remaining questions from seacliff?
[08:43] Ethan Cole: just one — how disruptive is switching a route to the quantized runtime for testing?
[08:47] Priya Nair: it's non-disruptive; we deploy traffic-split canaries and you can rollback instantly. quality and latency metrics are captured automatically.
[08:55] Maya Rodriguez: ok let's pilot quantized on background jobs first.
[09:00] [30:00] Jordan Lee: great. we'll recap action items now.
[09:05] Samir Patel: recap: jordan to send usage and invoice breakdown; priya to run dedicated pool benchmark; maya to provide usage export; samir to set weekly cadence; jordan to share SOC2 and SSO docs.
[09:20] Noah Bennett: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:25] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the deck and scheduling links.
[09:30] Maya Rodriguez: thanks, bye.
[09:32] [End of transcript]
